page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-512 is a flexible virtual machine instance positioned for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores across 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of RAM, establishing an elevated ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU (or 16.0 GB per physical core).

This instance profile features no integrated local storage and contains no discrete graphics processing hardware (0 GPUs). Consequently, persistent data operations rely on network-attached block volumes. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Architectural considerations require evaluating external storage throughput and latency profiles when planning disk-heavy workloads.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides substantial memory density, making the instance structurally cost-efficient for setups that require high memory allocations without paying for unnecessary excess compute cores. Dedicated physical core assignments avoid hypervisor contention, delivering deterministic performance across multi-threaded operations.

VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-512 is targeted at large-scale memory-optimized computing. Primary workload fits include enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caches, big data analytics engines, enterprise application runtimes, and large memory-bound container deployments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-512 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a dense 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and operates without GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for stateful workloads. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. By pairing dedicated AMD compute cores with an expanded memory pool, VM.Standard.E6.Flex.32-512 offers an efficient resource footprint for memory-bound applications without forcing over-provisioning of CPU resources. It is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, data processing frameworks, and heavy enterprise workloads.
